why: Both fix a failure; no alternative removes it without a rewrite. envload (9-21): a case-sensitivity false-absence bug; a dotenv parser may be better-tested than this ~20-line parser but lacks case-insensitive matching and the redacted CLI, so most of 196 lines stay -- under the house "hundreds of lines" bar. A typed-settings package wants a schema, wrong shape. quota (2-19): needs an exact UTC-midnight reset plus a durable JSONL trail. The limiter has no file store; decorator/retry packages don't persist or track quotas; closest is rolling-window -- different semantics, plus a file-lock dep.

alternatives.name: python-dotenv
alternatives.covers: Parsing of KEY=VALUE .env lines (quotes, comments, export prefix) -- the ~20-line _LINE/_unquote pair in envload.py, lines 47-68.
alternatives.gap: dotenv_values is case-sensitive by default per its own docs; no multi-file, cross-repo, case-insensitive candidate-name search, or fingerprint-only CLI.
alternatives.cost: ~30-40 lines removed, 1 dependency added; ~155 lines of candidate/case/CLI logic stay as-is.
alternatives.maturity: Long-standing, widely used; PyPI page checked this session, not installed here.

alternatives.name: pydantic-settings
alternatives.covers: Typed settings loaded from env vars plus a declared list of .env file paths, env vars overriding file values.
alternatives.gap: Wants a fixed schema of named fields, not "try 5 misspelled names across 2 repos, report only if found"; same manual glue needed either way per its own docs.
alternatives.cost: Would replace nearly the whole module's shape, not just parsing; not a line-count win.
alternatives.maturity: Actively maintained (Pydantic project); docs checked this session, not installed here.

alternatives.name: limits (alisaifee/limits)
alternatives.covers: Rate-limiting strategies (fixed/moving window) with a documented hit/test/get_window_stats API.
alternatives.gap: Its own docs list only Redis, Memcached, MongoDB as storage backends -- no file-based store, so persistence for solo CLI runs still needs a hand-written Storage backend.
alternatives.cost: Would not shrink quota.py meaningfully; adds a dependency for the algorithm only.
alternatives.maturity: Actively maintained per GitHub; docs checked this session, not installed here.

alternatives.name: ratelimit
alternatives.covers: In-process decorator that throttles calls to a Python function within one run.
alternatives.gap: No persistence across separate CLI invocations at all -- cannot enforce a daily ceiling across independent process runs, quota.py's core job.
alternatives.cost: Not usable as a replacement without adding the same file-backed state quota.py already has.

alternatives.name: tenacity
alternatives.covers: Retry/backoff policies (exponential wait, retry-on-exception) for a single call site.
alternatives.gap: Not a quota tracker at all -- no daily-ceiling concept, no persistence; solves retrying-after-failure, not refusing-before-the-ceiling.
alternatives.cost: Could complement quota.py for 429 backoff, but replaces none of its 121 lines.
alternatives.maturity: Very mature, widely used for retry logic specifically.

alternatives.name: pyrate-limiter
alternatives.covers: A leaky-bucket/rolling-window limiter with an optional SQLite-backed bucket for cross-process persistence, per its own docs.
alternatives.gap: Documented as leaky-bucket: Duration.DAY is a rolling window, not a fixed UTC-midnight reset -- the semantic quota.py's docstring says matters; multi-process safety needs an added file-lock dependency.
alternatives.cost: ~60-80 lines removed (lines 49-84) + 2 dependencies, but calendar-day and JSONL-audit properties need rebuilding on top.
alternatives.maturity: Actively maintained per PyPI/readthedocs checked this session; not installed or run here.

evidence: Read both files in full. Both wired, not orphaned: grep -n for each name in tools/dolt/client.py and tools/openrouter/client.py shows live imports/call sites before every request. No dedicated tests exist for either module; the one hit in tests/test_codemap.py only stubs the path for an unrelated test. Alternatives per WebSearch this session (their docs/PyPI pages), not installed or run here.
recheck: Check current release pages for the four rate-limit and two settings packages named below; read the persistent-bucket package's day-duration code directly, not its docs, to confirm rolling vs calendar-day reset.
migration_loc: envload: dotenv wrap cuts ~30-40 parsing lines (47-68) +1 dep, keeps ~155 candidate/case lines. quota: persistent-bucket lib cuts ~60-80 lines (49-84) +2 deps, drops JSONL trail/reset unless rebuilt.
what_ours_does: envload.py (196 ln): case-insensitive secret lookup across ordered candidate .env paths in a sibling repo, with misspelling fallbacks, and a presence/length/fingerprint-only CLI that never prints values. quota.py (121 ln): append-only JSONL usage ledger + DailyQuota (remaining/guard/pace/record) enforcing a UTC-day request ceiling, used by openrouter/client.py and dolt/client.py before every call.
strongest_counterargument: Working code is a weak guarantee: envload's parser (61-68) has no test and could mis-split a credential on an edge case an off-the-shelf parser has absorbed already. quota's 429-doesn't-count assumption (69-72) is itself unverified; one third-party, non-provider source found this session says failed attempts do count, which would mean quota overcounts remaining() regardless of library.
